correctness.rationale: The all-length proof is a bijective factorization of pairs (host,target) using greedy full-alphabet arches, with a unique last letter per arch and a fixed ambient alphabet. An absent shortest target has exactly one greedy match in each completed arch and none in the incomplete suffix. Exhaustive terminal-letter cases give diagonal and off-diagonal transition series; explicit full-support inclusion-exclusion and the symmetric matrix row sum prove the rational generating function. The ternary polynomial identity is exact. Dominance of the unique positive aperiodic renewal pole proves the mean asymptotic. Independent finite direct enumeration of 17,349 source words, arch pair counts and 36 ternary coefficients agrees. Finite checks are not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The theorem determines a natural average-case output-size invariant for missing scattered subsequences on every fixed alphabet \(q\ge3\) and for every host length. It gives the first nonbinary explicit rational mean with a fifth-order recurrence and a rigorous exponential expected-size growth law. Average-case complexity is not determined by existing per-word algorithms, binary-only means or extremal bounds. The extra off-diagonal terminal class and inclusion-exclusion renewal are substantive, rather than a relabeling or isolated low-n table.
